user_decision.question: Now that local llama3.1 inference is measured (viable only under named conditions: typical Sapience chunks fit within the client's 180s call timeout, but the client's own documented dense-chunk case still exceeds it at every thread setting measured), should programs.sapience.backend stay "anthropic" or flip to "ollama"?
options: Keep backend = "anthropic" — status quo: metered per-call cost, raw transcript text leaves this machine for a third-party provider, but every call completes reliably within its own timeout budget.

Flip backend = "ollama" (run via --backfill/interactive, not the scheduled 1-thread sync default) — no metered cost, raw transcript text stays confined to this machine, but a sufficiently dense chunk will occasionally time out and fail outright at the measured decode rate.
user_decision.recommended: Flip backend = "ollama" (run via --backfill/interactive, not the scheduled 1-thread sync default) — no metered cost, raw transcript text stays confined to this machine, but a sufficiently dense chunk will occasionally time out and fail outright at the measured decode rate.
user_decision.obligation: Discharges the privacy-confinement obligation docs/sapience.md's 'Why this backend' section names as the reason to revisit the anthropic choice at all: raw transcript text no longer leaves this machine for a third-party provider. The measured risk it accepts in exchange is a bounded, occasional per-chunk call failure on dense chunks specifically (Phase 3 of records/01_controlled-benchmark.md), not data loss or a broken pass — a failed chunk is simply not ingested that run.
